title: The Magpie and the Stolen Compass
story: Vessinor the Gust Magpie snatches the mapmaker's brass compass right off the canyon rim and flaps away laughing. By the time Mr 6 whistles up his kite-hawk, the thief already has a 9-league head start down the windy gorge. Mr 6 doesn't flap harder — he thinks faster.
question: Vessinor flies at a steady 12 leagues per hour, Mr 6's kite-hawk flies at 18 leagues per hour, and the magpie's head start is 9 leagues. How many hours until Mr 6 catches up?
solution: Each hour Mr 6 closes the gap by 18 - 12 = 6 leagues.
The gap is 9 leagues, so the time is 9 ÷ 6 = 1.5.
praise: Dividing the head start was the right instinct — the missing step was dividing by the CATCH-UP speed (18 - 12), not by one bird's speed alone.
hint: Don't ask how fast each bird flies — ask how much of the 9-league gap disappears in one hour.
victory: Exactly ninety minutes later Mr 6 glides alongside the startled magpie and politely holds out a hand; Vessinor drops the compass, squawks 'that was MATH, that was cheating!' and flaps off to steal something less well-guarded.
imagePrompt: A glossy black-and-silver magpie clutching a brass compass racing down a sunlit red canyon, pursued by a caped numeral-6 knight riding a kite-shaped hawk through swirling updrafts.
